neighbours.label: 'to'/'from' marking the end or start of a journey back or home (back to Ames, returning from a game, home from work)
fire: After the final whistle, the fans began the long train journey back to Glasgow.
The nurse was cycling home from her night shift when she saw the crash.
We caught the last ferry back to the island just before dark.
The soldiers were flying home from their tour in Afghanistan.
He hitchhiked all the way back to Memphis with a broken guitar.
The couple were returning from their honeymoon when the flight was delayed.
Every evening she walks back to the farm along the canal.
The band was driving back from a gig in Leeds when the van broke down.
quiet: After the final whistle, the fans gave a loud ovation to the Glasgow players.
The nurse got a thank-you card from her patient after the night shift.
We wrote a letter to the island council about the ferry timetable.
The soldiers received medals from the general for their tour.
He sold his broken guitar to a dealer in Memphis.
The couple received a gift from their aunt for the honeymoon.
Every evening she sends an email to the farm manager.
The band got a cheque from the promoter for the gig in Leeds.

notes: Card: ' to' x13, ' from' x12 (bus back to Ames, walk back to Harlem, returning from a hockey game). Probe: 'bus ride back to Denver' 0.96, 'driving home from work' 0.61; 'sent the letter to' 0.13, 'taken from a survey' 0.00. Near misses use to/from in non-travel senses with the same places.
